findings.who: A married filer files separately (or as head of household while still married). Their spouse was on active duty in 2025, and the filer is a nonmilitary spouse who lives in New York with the service member under military orders while keeping a domicile in another state.
findings.why_no: The gate counts the spouse only 'on a joint return, your spouse'. On a separate return the filer truthfully answers about themselves and says no, so the spouse's active duty is never asked.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 30: 'Note: Special rules under the SCRA apply to members of the military and their spouses for determining residency.'
findings.fix: Ask on every return: 'Since the start of 2022, did you or your spouse (whether or not you file jointly) serve in the U.S. armed forces, the reserves or the National Guard?' Treat a spouse's 2025 active duty as ending the New York part on any filing status.

findings.who: A cadet or midshipman at a federal service academy (for example West Point in New York) whose domicile is in another state. They live at the academy for more than 183 days in 2025.
findings.why_no: They read 'serve in the U.S. armed forces' as service after commissioning or enlistment, not academy attendance. Yet academy cadets are legally on active duty, so the active-service exception to the statutory resident test applies to them.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 30, Resident: 'whether or not you were domiciled in New York State (unless you were in active service in the military)'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Include service academy cadets and midshipmen, the Coast Guard, and reservists or Guard members called to active duty.'

findings.who: A commissioned officer of the U.S. Public Health Service or NOAA Corps (or the spouse of one) on active service in 2025.
findings.why_no: These uniformed services are not 'the U.S. armed forces, the reserves or the National Guard', so the filer truthfully answers no. The SCRA residency rules that the instructions point to still cover them.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 30: 'Special rules under the SCRA apply to members of the military and their spouses for determining residency.'
findings.fix: Widen the gate to 'the U.S. armed forces (including the Coast Guard), the reserves, the National Guard, or the Public Health Service or NOAA commissioned corps'. Route a yes for these services to the same out-of-scope stop.

findings.who: A Coast Guard member stationed in New York in 2025 who keeps a domicile in another state.
findings.why_no: They think of the Coast Guard as part of Homeland Security rather than 'the armed forces' and answer no.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 30, Resident: '(unless you were in active service in the military)'
findings.fix: Name the Coast Guard explicitly in the gate question.

used.revision: Form IT-201-I (2025), Instructions for Form IT-201 (including instructions for Forms IT-195 and IT-201-ATT), 41 pages; final 2025 edition; PDF modified 2025-11-20
locators: p. 30, Resident, "whether or not you were domiciled in New York State (unless you were in active service in the military)"

findings.who: A New York City or State employee who retired or left in 2024. In 2025 they received retroactive contract pay (arrears) on a 2025 Form W-2, with 414(h) contributions withheld and shown on it.
findings.why_no: They did not work for any government in 2025, so 'In 2025, did you ... work for the government in New York' is truthfully no.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 8, Line 21: 'enter the amount of 414(h) retirement contributions, if shown on any federal Form W-2 ... if you are: – a member of the New York City Employees' Retirement System ...'
findings.fix: Ask about the W-2, not the year worked: 'Does any 2025 Form W-2 (yours or, on a joint return, your spouse's) come from a New York public employer, or show 414(h) in box 14?' Include back pay from a job you have left.

findings.who: A New York public employee in the State or City retirement systems who works for an employer they don't think of as 'the government'. Examples: a nurse at NYC Health + Hospitals, a fire district, a public library, a housing or water authority, BOCES, or the Port Authority (bi-state).
findings.why_no: The help lists the State, cities, counties, towns, villages, school districts, SUNY/CUNY and 'public authorities such as the MTA'. A hospital, library, special district or bi-state agency doesn't look like it is on that list.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 8, Line 21: 'Are you a public employee of New York State or its local governments? ... a member of the New York State and Local Retirement Systems ... the New York City Employees' Retirement System ...'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Includes any employer whose staff belong to NYSLRS, NYSTRS, NYCERS, the NYC teachers', police or fire pension funds, or MABSTOA, such as public hospitals, libraries, fire districts, BOCES and the Port Authority. If box 14 of your W-2 shows 414(h), answer yes.'

findings.who: An employee of a New York State or New York City public employer who lives and works outside New York State, for example remotely from New Jersey or at a State office out of state. They are a member of a New York retirement system.
findings.why_no: They read 'work for the government in New York' as describing where the work is done, not who the employer is.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 8, Line 21: 'Are you a public employee of New York State or its local governments?'
findings.fix: Reword to 'was your employer New York State or a New York local government or public authority (wherever you worked)?'

findings.who: A chapter 11 debtor who is a New York public employee and allocates their Form W-2 wages to the bankruptcy estate. The tool may not count that W-2 on the individual return.
findings.why_no: The computed gate counts the Forms W-2 entered for line 1a. If the W-2 is allocated away and not entered, the count is zero and the question is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 23: 'you ... must allocate between you and the bankruptcy estate the wages ... reported to you on Form W-2.'
findings.fix: Count every Form W-2 received, including any allocated in whole or part to a bankruptcy estate, when computing scope.has_w2.

locators: p. 23, Line 1a, "Enter the total amount from Form(s) W-2, box 1"
